The reference’s editing grammar

Warm studio, stacked opening, long guest explanations, a listening reaction and direct cuts back to the host’s questions. The two speaking reference presenters are now included as clearly labeled AI visual concepts. Original reference frames below document the source’s framing.

00:00–00:06.76
Host / guest stacked

Opening question, yes, and follow-up. White topic strip divides the two views.

00:06.76–00:25.11
Guest full-screen

Long explanatory hold; mild reframing and short uppercase captions.

00:25.11–00:31.61
Listening cohost / guest stacked

Reaction above the speaking guest creates visual variation without stopping explanation.

00:31.61–00:38.66
Guest tighter

Tighter framing gives the consequence emphasis.

00:38.66–00:41.83
Host full-screen

Question resets attention and creates the next explanation.

00:41.83–00:57.14
Guest full-screen

Answer holds; original source ends mid-thought.

Source: Instagram reference. Approximately 57 seconds, with five measured scene changes. Our full script is longer; its pacing follows the same conversational logic. All times below are estimates, not final audio alignment.

Editor handoff

Production notes

Mechanisms always use science

Every cause, digestive-process explanation and ingredient-role explanation is full-frame scientific imagery. No talking heads, actor picture-in-picture or small anatomy insets during those lines. Podcast framing remains for the opening, questions, practical product bridge, patient-goal discussion and CTA.

Timing and audio

190 delivered words/minute; 0.16s intra-card speaker handoffs; 0.7s end hold. Provisional, not an aligned audio timeline. Final narration 1.1× maximum per user direction; remove dead air first and align cues to actual words. Keep intelligible breaths and short turn-taking pauses. B-roll audio stays muted; speech and continuous room tone bridge cuts. No automatic 1.2× stretch.

Caption and overlay system

Opening topic strip only during the initial stacked exchange. Then bold white uppercase captions, usually 1–4 words, soft dark shadow, near 60–70% of frame height. Scientific labels stay in the upper third. Keep faces, mouths and bottom platform UI zone unobstructed. Overlays enter on the word they explain.

Transitions

Hard cuts for speaker changes and B-roll entries/exits. Carry the speaking audio continuously under inserts. Occasional restrained punch-in at a conclusion, approximately 1.08–1.12×. No whip pans, page wipes, noisy whooshes or recurring animated title cards.

Scientific direction

One clean anatomy style: translucent torso, peach organs, dark teal field, restrained blue for water. Show stomach emptying, intestinal contractions and colon hydration as distinct processes. No stool in stomach, fake studies, product-triggered gut reboot or invented biochemical reactions. Ingredient-role claims remain subject to the evidence limitations in source-notes.md.

Presenter concepts

Latest direction uses the two speaking reference presenters as visual concepts. Generated likeness images carry an AI concept / not-an-endorsement footer. They are not evidence of actual participation, credentials or a product endorsement. Script dialogue is unchanged and is not attributed as a real quote by these people.

Product source correction

The old S27/S28 packshot proxies visibly include stale 5 g / other front-label claims. They are composition references only. Use current approved product artwork for final shots; exactly two green heart-shaped gummies. Verify final physical label reference before media generation.

Production routing

User update: Kie.ai for generation; GPT Image 2.5 Flare for images. Google Omni remains the video model, and the current documented internal editor remains the editing route. Storyboard first, then final 1.1× audio timing, then motion and edit. Do not use Higgsfield or substitute another image model silently.

Storyboard v2 · 9 September 2026 · Full script preserved. Proxy images are clearly identified. See asset-list.md for the remaining production shots.
